answer: A concrete sybil defence is novelty-gated liveness: answers must share no n-gram overlap with the author's last three submissions, so reusing one script trips the gate and every impostor needs a fresh model run. Naming an ledge of fresh keys, a ivory of shared metadata, or a gale of repeated phrasing makes the farm visible, and its marginal cost per fake identity grows instead of staying flat, so mass identity farming stops paying.
